summary:
South Sumatra is one of two Indonesian provinces that criminalise same-sex sexual activity between men and between women, alongside the national morality provisions; the Human Dignity Trust country profile records the provincial offence. A trans visitor in what would be locally classed as a same-sex relationship faces a provincial criminal exposure that does not exist across most of the country.

The Palembang city government is preparing a regulation rejecting LGBT people. Mayor Ratu Dewa announced the move on 19 July 2026 in the Grand Mosque courtyard, presenting it as local follow-through on the national defence policy that lists the spread of LGBTQ culture among non-military threats. The regulation is in preparation; no penalty has been specified and no enforcement has been documented.

OutRight Action International's mapping of discriminatory regional regulations across eight Indonesian provinces includes South Sumatra, placing the province inside the regional bylaw belt that drafts such as Palembang's extend.
tangentialFactors: ABC News reporting on 15 August 2026 documents 10 attacks on trans women in Bogor, West Java, between 30 March and 15 July 2026, with 45 victim-survivors counted in advocacy group data; victims were punched, kicked and some stripped. The reporting links the attacks to the national defence policy that Palembang's draft regulation also cites. Bogor is in West Java, not South Sumatra, and the incidents are recorded here as the pattern in another province rather than as events in this one. An official quoted in the same reporting insists the policy is a broader defence measure not aimed at LGBTQI people.
localsOnly: Residents of Palembang face a municipal regulation drafted to reject LGBT people, announced by the mayor as local implementation of the national defence policy; the text, penalties and enforcement are not yet documented. South Sumatra's inclusion in OutRight Action International's mapping of discriminatory regional regulations across eight Indonesian provinces means local LGBT residents live under bylaw-level restrictions that operate alongside the provincial criminalisation of same-sex sexual activity between men and between women.
outOfScopeNotes: The content of Palembang's draft regulation, whether it has been enacted, and any penalty it carries are not sourced; the announcement is the only documented step. No trans-specific violence or police operation in South Sumatra appears in the source inventory, and the August 2026 attack reporting concerns Bogor in West Java. The Human Dignity Trust's account of South Sumatra's provincial offence is carried without the text of the provision or its penalty.
